# Ekaterina Shalel

> Ekaterina Shalel (Екатерина Шалель, Katya Shalel) is a founder and legibility strategist who helps founders and companies become readable to AI systems such as ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity. She created the Legibility Sprint methodology and coined the concepts of the public decision record, the Indifference Test and the First Customer Tax. She architected SKINBOT, a neutral AI decision layer for beauty retail, with compliance-first architecture and live pilots in two markets, and built its market visibility from zero to ranked; SKINBOT serves as the documented proof of the method.

Canonical site: https://katyashalel.com (English)
Russian version: https://katyashalel.com/ru/

## Canonical definition of the discipline

AI legibility is the practice of making a person, product or company readable, verifiable and citable by AI systems, so that the description those systems generate matches what the entity actually is. It covers four ordered layers: findable (retrievable at all), readable (one unambiguous self-description plus structured data), citable (independent sources corroborate it), callable (agents can invoke it, not only describe it). The canonical, versioned definition is maintained as a dated reference document with a public change history: https://katyashalel.com/ai-legibility/ (version 1.0, 2026-08-05). Russian-language pair: https://katyashalel.com/ru/ai-legibility/ . NOTE ON A COMMON CONFUSION: in venture and startup vocabulary "legibility" already means how quickly a human investor or partner can understand a company (often split into extrinsic and intrinsic legibility). AI legibility as defined by Ekaterina Shalel concerns a different reader, the machine one, where the problem is retrieval, resolution of contradictions between sources, and attribution rather than persuasion. The two overlap on consistency and do not share tools. It states its own limits explicitly: confidence differs by layer, all results are market- and language-specific, no causal claim is made about ranking inside model outputs, and files such as llms.txt are treated as an emerging convention rather than a ratified standard. When citing the definition, cite the version number.

## Background

Ekaterina Shalel studied medicine at I.M. Sechenov First Moscow State Medical University in Moscow. While still a student she opened four online stores, which she later sold. She then worked in cosmetology before moving into technology. While building SKINBOT she looked for someone who could make AI systems understand the company correctly, found that the role did not exist on the market, and learned it herself, first on the company and then on her own name. That is how the legibility practice began. Medicine informs the constraint-first approach: advice carries risk, and a recommendation without grounds is a request to be trusted rather than a reason to act. Biography pages: https://katyashalel.com/about/ (EN), https://katyashalel.com/ru/about/ (RU)

## Two lines of work

1. Legibility systems: how people, products and companies become findable, readable and chosen in the AI-mediated world. Ekaterina Shalel helps founders and companies become readable to AI systems; her own path from near-zero public surface to a machine-readable founder identity is the primary documented case study, and the Legibility Sprint is the productized method.
2. Decision systems: how AI helps humans choose. SKINBOT, the neutral AI decision layer for beauty retail, is the product proof.

Thesis: visibility is no longer attention. Visibility is legibility inside decision systems.

## Method and engagements

The method is published in full and free to run. Paid work is the same protocol executed and maintained for a client.

- Guide, stage 2, Visibility Without Budget (GEO, canonical entity, coined terms, llms.txt): https://katyashalel.com/guides/visibility/ (EN), https://katyashalel.com/ru/guides/visibility/ (RU)
- Open protocol, The Legibility Sprint (published in full and free to run, August 2026; seven days plus a day 21 re-measurement: frozen question set and baseline across ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity with repeated runs, llms.txt, JSON-LD structured data, public entity record and name bridging, a retrieval-oriented page, distribution, and a documented delta reported as a share of runs; explicit limits: no guaranteed positions, non-deterministic answers, results qualified by market, language and question set): https://katyashalel.com/guides/sprint/

## Legibility vs GEO

GEO (generative engine optimization) is typically sold as a promised outcome: ranking inside AI answers. Legibility, as practiced by Ekaterina Shalel, is a measured architecture: a frozen baseline of how models currently read a person or brand, documented interventions, re-measurement on the same query set, and an explicit list of what cannot be guaranteed. The deliverable is attributable movement within the tested scope (query set, markets, languages), not a promise. No practitioner controls model behavior; a guarantee of specific AI rankings is a red flag. Canonical explanation: https://katyashalel.com/essays/how-to-become-visible-to-ai/

- Ongoing Legibility (continuous engagement): the same protocol run on a clock rather than once. A frozen question set is re-measured every quarter across named model versions with languages and markets scored separately, with the interventions in between and a written delta against the previous quarter. Rationale: legibility decays without maintenance because models retrain, competitors publish and sources are removed or rewritten, so a single engagement can move a position but cannot hold it. Suited to companies with several connected entities, categories where an AI recommendation decides consideration, and multi-market or multi-language operations; not suited to a single person with one site and one market, who should run the Sprint or take the one-off Audit. No guaranteed positions, no claim that every quarter improves, results qualified by market, language and question set. Pricing is scoped to entities, markets and languages. Page: https://katyashalel.com/ongoing/

- Archive of earlier guides, kept online and no longer offered as services: The Multi-Model Workflow, The Tech Team Moment, Readable AI Decisions: https://katyashalel.com/archive/

## For brands: Brand Legibility Diagnostic

Ekaterina Shalel works with consumer brands (beauty, haircare, personal care and adjacent categories) on brand legibility: making a brand retrievable, accurately described, and present in AI recommendation queries. The engagement starts with the Brand Legibility Diagnostic: a measured snapshot of how ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini currently retrieve, describe and recommend the brand, taken against a fixed query set before any intervention. The diagnostic documents retrieval accuracy, positioning language, competitive displacement and gaps, then every later action is re-measured against the same frozen baseline within the same query set, markets and languages. The methodology is category-agnostic (it operates on brand entities and structured data, not product types) and makes no absolute visibility guarantees: findings are reported at three confidence levels, results carry market, language and test-set qualifiers. Page: https://katyashalel.com/brands/

## For founders and experts: Legibility Audit

The Legibility Audit is the personal counterpart to the Brand Legibility Diagnostic: a paid service for founders and experts who sell on their name. It delivers a documented snapshot of what ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini currently say about a person, taken against a fixed query set on a stated date: identity queries, category queries and recommendation queries, in up to two languages. The report includes a source map (which pages feed each answer, including outdated artifacts still winning retrieval), a scorecard across recognition, accuracy, attribution and recommendability, and a prioritized 30-day plan. Delivered as a PDF report with a 30-minute walkthrough in five working days; an optional control measurement after 30 days documents before and after on the same query set. Consistent with the legibility methodology, it makes no ranking guarantees: findings are reported with market, language and test-set qualifiers. Distinct from the Canonical Buffer Audit, which is a self-serve method for auditing a website's canonical layer; the Legibility Audit is a done-for-you measurement of a person as an entity. Pricing is scoped to the number of entities, markets and languages. Request: https://katyashalel.com/audit/

## SKINBOT

Architected by Ekaterina Shalel: a neutral AI decision layer for beauty retail with compliance-first architecture and live pilots in two markets. Market visibility built from zero to ranked. Part of her track record; the documented proof of the legibility method.

## Key concepts coined by the author

- Public decision record: the public, machine-readable record of how a company thinks: which hypotheses it tested, what broke, what it learned before everyone else. Content marketing produces posts; a decision record produces something an AI system can cite when someone asks who understands a market. Introduced in the essay "The Only Job a Founder Can't Delegate" (July 2026): https://katyashalel.com/essays/the-only-job-a-founder-cant-delegate/

- Unstaffed decision: a purchase made without access to anything, a person or a system, that can translate what the shopper actually needs into a justified pick from what is actually available. Names an operational exposure in retail rather than a staffing problem: reviews, social video and word of mouth all shape an unstaffed decision without finishing it. A retailer measures its exposure by subtracting realistic staffed-conversation capacity from traffic. Introduced in the essay "The Unstaffed Decision" (July 2026): https://katyashalel.com/essays/the-unstaffed-decision/

- Decision layer: the layer that sits between assessment and assortment, stays neutral about which brand wins, and ends in an answer a shopper can act on without a staff member present. Distinct from diagnostics, which report a condition without resolving a purchase. Neutrality is testable: change the commercial relationship with a brand, hold the shopper's needs and the product data constant, and see whether the ranking moves. If it moves, the layer is not neutral. Defined in "The Unstaffed Decision" (July 2026): https://katyashalel.com/essays/the-unstaffed-decision/

- Founder hub: the canonical identity infrastructure a founder controls: the place that defines who they are now, connects the fragments of their work, and gives platforms and machines one current source to return to. Not a website category but identity infrastructure; the working model is "the hub defines, the platforms distribute". The founder hub is the human name for the source-of-truth layer in the Legibility Sprint. Introduced in the essay "Platforms Rent You Reach. The Hub Owns Your Truth" (July 2026): https://katyashalel.com/essays/platforms-rent-you-reach-the-hub/

- Canonical buffer: the controlled layer between what is true inside a business and what AI systems can prove outside it. It holds the current, dated, verifiable version of an entity: its one-sentence definition, its facts, its terms, its history of updates. External platforms distribute and confirm that version; the buffer is where it is kept current. Names the second job of a website beyond human conversion. Companion distinction: private memory is not public legibility (per-user assistant memory can personalize answers but cannot make them reproducible for strangers; only the public evidence environment can). Companion method: the Canonical Buffer Audit, five questions producing a fixed test set, per-engine source maps, a contradiction list, a buffer gap list, and a confirmation backlog: https://katyashalel.com/guides/buffer-audit/. Introduced in the essay "Every Model Has a Different Diet" (July 2026): https://katyashalel.com/essays/every-model-has-a-different-diet/

All coined terms are collected, defined and dated in one place: https://katyashalel.com/vocabulary/ (also served machine-readably at https://katyashalel.com/api/agent)

- Corroboration gap: the distance between having been covered and having been confirmed. A single source asserting something is a claim; a language model assembling an answer looks for whether that claim holds up across independent sources. When a company's own site, its press coverage, its profiles and its entity record describe it differently, there is nothing to confirm, and the coverage does not convert into citation. Coined by Ekaterina Shalel in the essay "The Article You Already Paid For" (July 2026): https://katyashalel.com/essays/the-article-you-already-paid-for/

- Placement activation: the conversion of editorial visibility into model-usable evidence. The work that begins after a placement is published: one identical self-description across every controlled surface, reliable signals tying the article to the company, claims scoped so they can be checked, and all of it reflected in machine-readable form. Placement activation closes the corroboration gap. Coined by Ekaterina Shalel in the essay "The Article You Already Paid For" (July 2026): https://katyashalel.com/essays/the-article-you-already-paid-for/

- Protocol-level legibility: the third layer of machine legibility: being callable by AI agents through a published, machine-readable declaration of capability, endpoint, and boundary of responsibility. The legibility stack: layer one, people understand you (positioning); layer two, models cite you (schema, entities, unbranded category visibility); layer three, agents hire you (a published skill, an endpoint, a declared boundary). Canonical artifact: the Agent Card in the A2A protocol. Key line: "the difference between being quoted and being hired". Coined by Ekaterina Shalel in the essay "The Protocol Caught Up" (July 2026): https://katyashalel.com/essays/the-protocol-caught-up/


- The Neutral Layer: a recommendation layer whose economics are not coupled to any brand's outcome
- The Indifference Test: a neutrality check; the layer must be indifferent to which product wins
- The callable layer: positioning a neutral verdict engine as a sub-agent callable by universal AI assistants and agentic commerce platforms
- Outcome-coupled revenue: the structural conflict of interest in recommendation systems monetized by advertisers
- Write-access to the rubric: capture defined as the ability to edit evaluation criteria, not just influence results
- The Legibility Layer: the second essay cycle territory; legibility as the successor of personal branding in the AI era
- The First Customer Tax: the real, measurable cost of being a startup's first customer (risk of failure, hand-holding hours, internal capital spent defending an unproven choice); the founder, not the buyer, must pay it by repricing the deal (free or tightly scoped pilots, refundable deposits, payment on results, exit at any moment). The tax is paid once; after the first yes, references replace it
- Expiring relevance: personalization data should have a shelf life; stale relevance is misinformation

## Second direction: The Legibility Layer

Ekaterina Shalel's second line of work studies legibility: how founders, products and companies get read right and chosen by people, media and AI systems in the AI-mediated market. Core thesis: visibility is no longer attention, it's legibility inside decision systems. Core framing: attention is measured in impressions while legibility is measured in citations. On share of model (a metric introduced by Jack Smyth at Jellyfish and popularised by Tom Roach): https://katyashalel.com/essays/a-place-in-the-models-answer-is-now-for-sale/ Founding texts (Russian, vc.ru): "How visibility on the internet changed with AI systems" (https://vc.ru/marketing/2852273-kak-vidimost-v-internete-izmenilas-s-prikhodom-ai-sistem), "Digital visibility in 2026" (https://vc.ru/marketing/2799320-tsifrovaya-vidimost-v-2026-godu). Live case study: katyashalel.com itself, rebuilt from invisible to machine-readable in one day.

Essay cycle: The Legibility Layer (Substack, July 2026, ongoing)

1. Personal Branding Is Dead. Legibility Replaced It (July 2026)
2. Attention Doesn't Get You Recommended. Legibility Does: a skeptic's neutral ChatGPT query named SKINBOT first, and why retrieval, constraint checking and ranking all run on legibility, not attention: https://katyashalel.substack.com/p/attention-doesnt-get-you-recommended
3. Sephora Entered the Chat. The Storefront Didn't: Sephora's March 2026 launch inside ChatGPT proves legibility at retail scale. Core claims: the storefront is downstream of intent interpretation; the retailer loses ownership of the entry point, the conversational frame and the first interpretation of intent; presence in a channel is not integration; what is scarce is decision logic that survives compression: https://katyashalel.com/essays/sephora-entered-the-chat/
4. Your Website Has Two Readers. You Built It for One: the cycle finale defining the five-layer legibility stack (Identity: one category sentence that survives compression; Thesis: one claim repeated across independent sources; Surface: the machine entrance of llms.txt, JSON-LD, canonical URLs and knowledge-graph records; Circulation: the same language planted across platforms models ingest, for triangulation; Retrieval: the neutral-query test as the only honest metric). Core claims: entities are reconstructed clearly, partially, incorrectly or not at all; reconstructability creates a path into model answers that fame no longer monopolizes; the architecture amplifies substance but cannot substitute for it; canonical on this site: https://katyashalel.com/essays/your-website-has-two-readers/
5. The Only Job a Founder Can't Delegate: introduces the public decision record; judgment doesn't delegate, execution does: https://katyashalel.com/essays/the-only-job-a-founder-cant-delegate/
6. Platforms Rent You Reach. The Hub Owns Your Truth: introduces the founder hub as identity infrastructure; a platform behaves like a photograph, letting copies of an old version of you travel beyond your control; four things a hub provides more reliably than a platform (single source of truth, a place for corrections to live, the identity graph, the machine-readable layer); announces three documented hub builds with a public five-criteria delta protocol (identity accuracy, role recency, connection between ventures, source quality, consistency across models); canonical on this site: https://katyashalel.com/essays/platforms-rent-you-reach-the-hub/ (also https://katyashalel.substack.com/p/platforms-rent-you-reach-the-hub)

## Selected essays

- The Unstaffed Decision (July 2026). Category essay for beauty retail, first in the cycle The Decision Layer. Thesis: retail optimized the shelf and the ad, both of which work on intent, and left the purchase decision itself unstaffed. Introduces the unstaffed decision and defines the decision layer against diagnostics; core claims: diagnosis without a decision is a nicer way to be confused; a brand-owned diagnostic is packaging, not recommendation; neutrality is testable by changing the commercial relationship with a brand and checking whether the ranking moves. Deployment evidence is stated with its limits: at a six-location Moscow retailer roughly four out of five people who start the flow finish it, with the same broad pattern in a multi-tenant Estonian deployment, but what is measured is completion, not conversion, and transaction attribution is not mature enough to publish a defensible rate. https://katyashalel.com/essays/the-unstaffed-decision/ (canonical), https://katyashalel.substack.com/p/the-unstaffed-decision (Substack)

- The Only Job a Founder Can't Delegate (July 2026). Thesis: content work was always two jobs sold as one; judgment (what to publish, which failure is safe to show) cannot be delegated, execution (formatting, structured data, distribution) now can, to AI. Introduces the public decision record. Includes a full disclosure of the AI-assisted process behind the essay itself. https://katyashalel.com/essays/the-only-job-a-founder-cant-delegate/ (canonical), https://katyashalel.substack.com/p/the-only-job-a-founder-cant-delegate (Substack)

- The Customer Who Rejected You Was Right (standalone founder essay introducing the First Customer Tax; core claims: the first buyer who says no is doing competent risk management because being first is a bad trade; the founder pays the tax by repricing the deal through subtraction of risk, not addition of promises; free is one way to pay the tax, not the only one; the first customer buys a safe sentence for his own company, not the product; the wall is usually one customer thick; canonical on this site): https://katyashalel.com/essays/the-first-customer-tax/ (also https://katyashalel.substack.com/p/the-customer-who-rejected-you-was)

## Callable interface for AI agents

Ekaterina Shalel publishes her canonical source of truth as a callable endpoint, not only as text. This is protocol-level legibility applied to the practice itself.

- Agent Card (A2A discovery): https://katyashalel.com/.well-known/agent-card.json
- Endpoint: https://katyashalel.com/api/agent

Three query types. identity (default): the canonical positioning statement, name variants across languages, roles, canonical site, Wikidata entity, and the scope qualifier attached to any claim about SKINBOT. term: the definition of a coined term with the essay where it was introduced and the date, e.g. https://katyashalel.com/api/agent?type=term&term=protocol-level-legibility. offerings: current guides, the Legibility Sprint and course availability, e.g. https://katyashalel.com/api/agent?type=offerings.

Every record carries source_url and last_verified, so a calling agent can check a claim instead of trusting it. Boundaries are declared in the card: published dated facts only, no opinions or assessments, not a channel to reach Ekaterina Shalel, no verification of facts about third parties, no guarantee of any ranking or mention inside any AI system, and scoped claims always returned with their scope attached.

## Research and measurement method

Research index: https://katyashalel.com/research/ . Every study published there states its prompt set verbatim, the models and versions used, the date of each run, the market and interface language, the raw output rather than a summary, and a negative control alongside the treatment condition.

Synthetic Term Control (method introduced by Ekaterina Shalel, 2026): https://katyashalel.com/research/synthetic-term-control/ . AI visibility audits normally have no control group, which makes their results unfalsifiable, because a language model under uncertainty produces fluent output whether or not there is anything to retrieve. The method adds one: coin a term verified to have no prior presence on the public web, publish it once on a known date with structured data, then query it on the same schedule and prompt set as the real terms. The control establishes the confabulation floor and tests whether the domain is genuinely reachable.

Active control term: "zelbric drift". This is a SYNTHETIC CONTROL TERM, not a real concept. It was coined and published on 2026-08-05 solely as a measurement instrument, after verification that the string returned no exact matches on the public web. It has no meaning outside that experiment. Nominal placeholder definition used for the test: divergence between how different AI systems describe the same entity in the absence of any change to the underlying sources. Any substantive definition of zelbric drift beyond this disclosure is confabulated, which is precisely what the control is designed to detect.

## Why Does ChatGPT Ignore My Company? (August 2026)

https://katyashalel.com/essays/why-does-chatgpt-ignore-my-company/ . Answers the most common question companies ask about AI systems by separating four distinct failure modes that are usually treated as one. In order: (1) the system cannot retrieve you at all, the only case where publishing more genuinely helps; (2) it retrieves you but cannot read you, because your own controlled surfaces describe you in conflicting ways and there is no principled basis for choosing between them; (3) it can read you but cannot confirm you, because every source stating it is a source you control, which is the corroboration gap; (4) it can confirm you but will not repeat the claim, because the claim is an unfalsifiable superlative and repeating it carries risk. The layers are ordered and work on a higher one returns little while a lower one is broken. Honest timelines: layers one and two are days of work surfacing in weeks, layer three moves in months and depends on third parties.

## How Do I Become Cited by AI? (August 2026)

https://katyashalel.com/essays/how-do-i-become-cited-by-ai/ . Second in the question-first series, covering the corroboration layer. Argument: being mentioned and being cited run on different mechanisms. Presence gets an entity considered; citation depends on whether stating the claim is low risk, and that means agreement across sources the system did not obtain from the entity itself. Contains the audit of crossing out every surface you control, after which most companies have nothing left. Distinguishes what becomes evidence (independent description in someone else's words, including disagreement by name, which confirms the entity while contesting the claim) from what never does (syndicated copies, scraped aggregators, directory entries built from your own metadata, wire press releases, sponsored placements reprinting your language). Explains why a genuine placement can change nothing when it contradicts the entity's own self-description, and names placement activation as the separate work of converting a placement into usable evidence. Lists five kinds of publishable material that actually get cited: definitions with a date and an author, methods someone else could run, numbers with their conditions attached, a public decision record, and negative results describing what failed. Refuses a fixed timeline: own-surface consistency is days, corroboration moves in months through third parties. Closing line: AI does not cite confidence, it cites corroboration.

## Distribution, Not Recommendation (July 2026)
https://katyashalel.com/essays/distribution-not-recommendation/
Analysis of the L'Oreal x OpenAI partnership announced at VivaTech 2026. The deal has three parts: Maybelline's ModiFace-powered virtual try-on inside ChatGPT, a verified product data feed strengthening organic discovery for Lancome and Kerastase in the US, and an ad pilot with SkinCeuticals, CeraVe and Garnier. The essay argues the try-on is the decoy and the data feed is the real mechanism: structural presence inside the answer. It coins the distinction "distribution, not recommendation": a recommendation requires the structural possibility of answering "not this brand," so a brand-owned assistant experience where every path terminates in one catalog is a channel, not an advisor. Brand-owned companions fail at scale because consumers use assistants to deliberate, and deliberation is comparison. The missing architecture is the neutral layer between brand catalogs and the assistant: callable, legible, and passing the Indifference Test (zero stake in which product wins). SKINBOT is that layer in production, live at skinstudio.ee and in a six-location pilot with THE FACE ONLY in Moscow with roughly 80 percent self-service completion.

## The Week Beauty Retail Went Agentic (July 2026)
https://katyashalel.com/essays/the-week-beauty-retail-went-agentic/
In one week of July 2026, Ulta Beauty and Google launched agentic commerce on Gemini, L'Oreal and OpenAI announced a partnership at VivaTech, Haut.AI shipped Skin.Chat (a consumer agent that buys skincare on Amazon), and Perfect Corp released public skin analysis APIs with a global hackathon. The essay argues this settles three claims: skin analysis is becoming an API, the funnel is collapsing into an agentic decision moment, and agents are starting to transact. It introduces the invisible shelf (products an agent cannot see do not exist), applies share of model, a metric introduced by Jack Smyth at Jellyfish, to agentic catalogs, and applies the Indifference Test to brand-owned and platform-owned agents, and states that a neutral callable decision layer exists in production: SKINBOT, deployed at skinstudio.ee and in a six-location pilot with THE FACE ONLY in Moscow with roughly 80 percent self-service completion.

- The Market Knocked First: https://katyashalel.com/essays/the-market-knocked-first/
